title: Intrinsic (valley) thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in graphene for integer quantum Hall phases
abstract: We calculate the intrinsic contribution to the (valley) thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in (Semenoff-gapped) graphene in the quantum Hall regime where bulk electron thermal transport is suppressed. The (valley) thermal Hall transport of phonons considered here originates from a phonon (valley) Hall viscosity induced by electron (valley) Hall conductivity and viscosity via geometric electron-phonon coupling. The so generated phonon (valley) Hall viscosity is identified with the emergent (valley) Hall viscosity recently introduced in \textit{Phys. Lett. A} \textbf{595}, 132096 (2026). While our calculations refer to graphene, they may very well be generalized to other Dirac materials like group-VI transition metal dichalcogenides. We discuss the prospect of measuring the phonon thermal Hall conductivity in graphene-based heterostructures and estimate the corresponding valley response induced by electrons in the inversion symmetry broken phase.
summary: This paper theoretically calculates the intrinsic thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in graphene operating in the quantum Hall regime. It shows that while the intrinsic phonon contribution is small, the valley-dependent phonon thermal Hall effect is predicted to be significant. The methodology relies on coupling electron Hall physics to lattice vibrations via emergent Hall viscosities.
main_problem: Calculating the intrinsic (valley) thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in graphene when bulk electron thermal transport is suppressed in the quantum Hall regime.
main_result: The intrinsic phonon thermal Hall transport is predicted to be very small compared to electron transport, but the valley thermal Hall transport is predicted to be comparable in size to the charge channel transport for Dirac materials.
method: The calculation uses a theoretical framework involving the phonon Berry curvature and the concept of phonon Hall viscosity, derived from geometric electron-phonon coupling.
model_or_system: The system is graphene modeled in the quantum Hall regime, treated as a Semenoff semiconductor. The analysis involves coupling acoustic phonons to Dirac fermions via lattice distortions.
key_observables: Phonon thermal Hall conductivity ($\kappa_{ph}^H$), Valley thermal Hall conductivity ($\kappa_{ph}^vH$), and Phonon Hall viscosity ($\eta_{	ext{em}}^H$).
important_parameters: Quantum Hall regime, low temperature limit ($T \ll T_{	ext{Debye}}$), and the valley degree of freedom.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the transverse phonon response originates from the intrinsic phonon Hall viscosity-induced mechanism and that graphene can be approximated by pristine graphene.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical link between phonon Hall viscosity and thermal transport, then deriving the phonon Berry curvature, and finally calculating the thermal Hall conductivity in the low-temperature and quantum Hall limits.
why_interesting: The work connects topological concepts (Hall viscosity, Berry curvature) from electronic transport to lattice vibrations (phonons), providing a mechanism to study valley physics in thermal transport, which is relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter.
